content.title: Paul Thomas Anderson Gave “Special Thanks” to Maya Rudolph at the Oscars 2026
content.text: Paul Thomas Anderson and his partner, Maya Rudolph, were both at the Oscars 2026—but they appeared on the Oscar stage separately. Anderson won best director, best adapted screenplay, and best picture for his film One Battle After Another, while Rudolph was there to present a pair of awards with the cast of her comedy Bridesmaids, celebrating its 15th anniversary this year.While the two sat together at the 98th Academy Awards, they took the stage separately, with Anderson mentioning her and their shared abode as he accepted the award for best adapted screenplay. First he thanked Thomas Pynchon, though, whose 1990 novel, Vineland, became the basis for the revolutionary film. “Any writer knows that you either beg for forgiveness or your special thanks is really to your family and the people that you share a roof with, who put up with what it means to live with a writer,” Anderson said as he looked out to Rudolph in the audience. “To Maya.”Anderson and Rudolph are not married, but they have four children together: Pearl, Lucille, Jack, and Minnie. (All four appeared in his 2021 movie, Licorice Pizza, which was filmed when COVID-19 restrictions kept social networks tight.)He also mentioned his children during his acceptance speech for the adapted-screenplay award on Sunday night. “I wrote this movie for my kids, to say sorry for the housekeeping mess that we left in this world we’re handing off to them,” Anderson said. “But also with the encouragement that they will be the generation that hopefully brings us some common sense and decency.”When Anderson took home the best-feature Gotham Award for One Battle After Another late last year, he mentioned his relationship with Rudolph and clarified when they first met. “December 1, 24 years ago, I met a lady who made me a better filmmaker,” he said. “Happy anniversary, Maya.”Rudolph is a comedian best known for her years on Saturday Night Live. Earlier this week she announced that she would be joining the cast of the Broadway show Oh, Mary! in the titular role. She was credited as an actor in Anderson’s 2014 film, Inherent Vice, and also appeared in Licorice Pizza as a casting director’s assistant.Watch the Vanity Fair Oscar Party livestream—hosted by Quenlin Blackwell, Jake Shane, and Brittany Broski—directly after the Academy Awards at youtube.com/vanityfair on Sunday, March 15 at 10:30 p.m. ET and 7:30 p.m. PT.The 14 Best-Dressed Stars at the 2026 OscarsMike Coppola/Getty ImagesTeyana TaylorIn the words of Tyla, “put me in Chanel!” Taylor looked stunning in a black-and-white concoction by Chanel designer Matthieu Blazy, which she paired with Tiffany & Co. jewelry.
